target: Det är skönt att vara ledig.
english: It's nice to be free.
tip: "Skönt" conveys comfort and relief – a very Swedish sensation word.

target: Hur som helst måste vi gå nu.
english: Anyway we must go now.
tip: Past endings: -ade (group 1, most regular), -de or -te (group 2). tittade (looked), läste (read), köpte (bought). Same form for every subject.

target: Brödet är nybakat.
english: The bread is freshly baked.
tip: "En" words: en bok (a book), boken (the book). "Ett" words: ett hus (a house), huset (the house).

target: Jag tar en kladdkaka.
english: I'll have a sticky chocolate cake.
tip: Kladdkaka is a beloved Swedish dessert – intentionally undercooked for gooey richness.

target: Det finns bröd på hyllan.
english: There is bread on the shelf.
tip: `det är` = 'it is / there is'. `Det finns` = 'there is/are' for existence. `Det är en bil` (it is a car) vs `det finns en bil` (there is a car).

target: Hittills har allt gått bra.
english: So far everything has gone well.
tip: Perfect tense uses `har + supinum`: `jag har talat`, `vi har sett`. The supinum is the form ending -at / -t / -tt / -it – distinct from past tense.

target: Vi har ett rum med utsikt.
english: We have a room with a view.
tip: "Rum" is ett-word: ett rum, rummet, rum, rummen.

target: Hon är mycket omtyckt av alla sina kollegor.
english: She is very well liked by all her colleagues.
tip: Swedish past tense has 4 verb groups with different endings: -ade, -de, -dde, irregular.

target: Ibland går vi ut och äter med familjen.
english: Sometimes we go out to eat with the family.
tip: "Ibland" = sometimes. Triggers V2 inversion like other fronted adverbs.

target: God kväll, hoppas du har haft en bra dag.
english: Good evening, I hope you've had a good day.
tip: 'Bra' (good) never changes form – it's the same in all positions. Comparative: 'bättre', superlative: 'bäst'.

target: Tack detsamma, när jag hörde de goda nyheterna idag!
english: Thanks, same to you, when I heard the good news today!
tip: Swedish adjectives agree with the noun's gender: "en stor bil" vs "ett stort hus".

target: Ett svart moln täckte solen och det blev plötsligt mörkt.
english: A black cloud covered the sun and it suddenly became dark.
tip: "By" is en-word: en by, byn, byar, byarna. Means village.

target: Det finns ett gammalt slott i parken som är från 1600-talet.
english: There is an old castle in the park that dates from the 1600s.
tip: "Gammal" → "gammalt" for ett-words.

target: En stad i norra Sverige.
english: A city in northern Sweden.
tip: "Norra" = northern. Compass adj: norra, södra, östra, västra.

target: De långa sommarkvällarna.
english: The long summer evenings.
tip: V2 word order is one of Swedish's core rules – it applies to every declarative main clause, regardless of what comes first.

target: Hej, hur mår du?
english: Hello, how are you?
tip: 'Hur' (how) – for manner/degree: 'Hur mår du?' (How are you?), 'Hur långt?' (How far?).

target: En bit av kakan.
english: A piece of cake.
tip: "Bit" = piece. "En bit av" = a piece of.

target: Året då allt förändrades.
english: The year when everything changed.
tip: The V2 rule doesn't apply in subordinate clauses (after att, som, när, etc.) – there the subject comes before the verb.

target: Vi gläds åt nyheten.
english: We rejoice at the news.
tip: When you front an adverb or object for emphasis, the verb must stay second – the subject simply moves to accommodate it.

target: Han lyser upp rummet.
english: He lights up the room.
tip: Unlike English, Swedish requires the verb in position two. When emphasis shifts the first element, the subject slides to third position.

target: En stol och ett bord.
english: A chair and a table.
tip: "Stol" is en-word, "bord" is ett-word. There's no pattern – just memorize them.

target: En sked och en gaffel.
english: A spoon and a fork.
tip: "Sked" (spoon) and "gaffel" (fork) are both en-words.

target: Tack vare dig lyckades vi.
english: Thanks to you we succeeded.
tip: Object pronouns: mig (me), dig (you), honom (him), henne (her), oss (us), er (you pl), dem (them). Place after the verb: `jag ser dig`.

target: Jag tar en lax med potatis.
english: I'll have salmon with potatoes.
tip: "Jag tar" (I'll take) is the most natural way to order at a restaurant.

target: Det finns ett brev till dig.
english: There is a letter for you.
tip: `det är` = 'it is / there is'. `Det finns` = 'there is/are' for existence. `Det är en bil` (it is a car) vs `det finns en bil` (there is a car).

target: Det är bara två dagar kvar.
english: There are only two days left.
tip: Swedish questions use V1 word order: verb first. "Talar du svenska?" = Do you speak Swedish?

target: Finns det en parkeringsplats i närheten?
english: Is there a parking space near here?
tip: "Parkeringsplats" = parking spot. Swedish compound: parkering + s + plats.

target: De har helt förändrat planen.
english: They have completely changed the plan.
tip: Perfect tense uses `har + supinum`: `jag har talat`, `vi har sett`. The supinum is the form ending -at / -t / -tt / -it – distinct from past tense.

target: Första maj är en röd dag.
english: May Day is a public holiday.
tip: "Röd dag" (red day) is the Swedish term for public holidays.

target: Buffén har mycket att välja på.
english: The buffet has a lot to choose from.
tip: Don't confuse supinum with the past tense. Past: `jag åt` (I ate). Perfect: `jag har ätit` (I have eaten). Same root, different endings, different uses.

target: Var är utgången på morgonen nog?
english: Where is the exit in the morning probably?
tip: In main clauses, sentence adverbs (inte, alltid, aldrig, redan) come right after the conjugated verb, not before it.

target: Hem gick vi tidigt i helgen här.
english: Home we went early on the weekend here.
tip: Adverb topicalization with V2 inversion.

target: Hur vi löser problemet vet jag inte.
english: How we solve the problem I don't know.
tip: Fronted indirect question as topic: "Hur vi löser" + inverted main: "vet jag inte."

target: Pingvinen simmar snabbt genom det iskalla vattnet.
english: The penguin swims quickly through the ice-cold water.
tip: "Mätt" means satisfied/full after eating – important at Swedish dinner parties.

target: Pojken som bor bredvid oss spelar trumpet.
english: The boy who lives next to us plays trumpet.
tip: In December in Stockholm, darkness falls as early as 3 PM.

target: Ett stort skepp låg i hamnen och väntade på passagerare.
english: A large ship was in the harbor waiting for passengers.
tip: Group 4 verbs change vowels instead of adding endings: dricka → drack (drink → drank), gå → gick (go → went), se → såg (see → saw). Common irregulars.

target: Inbjudan accepterades av alla.
english: The invitation was accepted by everyone.
tip: The V2 rule means if you start with something other than the subject, the subject must follow the verb: 'Igår köpte jag...' not 'Igår jag köpte...'

target: Det är en annan femma.
english: That's a different kettle of fish.
tip: "En annan femma" = a different five (coin) – a whole different story.

target: Såvida du inte ångrar dig.
english: Unless you change your mind.
tip: Swedish keeps the verb second in statements. Starting with an adverb or object forces the subject behind the verb.

target: Har ni något vegetariskt på kvällen gärna?
english: Do you have anything vegetarian in the evening gladly?
tip: "Ni" is used for addressing service staff, though "du" is also fine.

target: Vinodlaren skördade druvorna i september med familjen.
english: The winemaker harvested the grapes in September with his family.
tip: "På kvällen" = in the evening. Time phrases with "på" for parts of the day.

target: Hur gammal är du?
english: How old are you?
tip: Swedish only has one 'you' in modern use: `du`. Use it with strangers, your boss, the king – everyone. The formal `Ni` is essentially extinct outside very formal letters.

target: I princip är vi överens.
english: In principle, we agree.
tip: If anything but the subject opens the sentence, the subject inverts after the verb – V2 rule. `Idag äter jag pizza` (today eat I pizza). Same rule as German/Dutch.

target: Den nya lägenheten är stor.
english: The new apartment is big.
tip: Double definite: "Den nya lägenheten" – article + adjective-a + noun-definite.

target: Jag gick till affären igår.
english: I went to the store yesterday.
tip: "Gå" is irregular in past tense: gå → gick. Many common verbs are irregular.

target: Vad jag tycker spelar ingen roll.
english: What I think doesn't matter.
tip: Subordinate clause as subject – placed first with no inversion in the main clause.

target: Klockan är fem i halv tre.
english: It is five minutes to half past two.
tip: "Fem i halv tre" = five to half-three = 2:25. Swedish time can be confusing!

target: I Stockholm bor det många människor också.
english: In Stockholm live many people too.
tip: "Det" is an expletive (filler) subject. The real subject follows the verb.

target: Trevligt att träffas, jag är ny här.
english: Nice to meet you, I'm new here.
tip: 'Ny' (new): en→ny, ett→nytt, definite/plural→nya. The -tt ending marks neuter.

target: Vad fint väder det är idag nog!
english: What lovely weather we're having today!
tip: Exclamation pattern: "Vad" + adjective + noun + "det är"!

target: I Sverige är sommaren kort.
english: In Sweden the summer is short.
tip: Place phrases trigger V2: "I Sverige" (1st) + "är" (2nd) + "sommaren" (3rd).

target: Vederbörande har inte lämnat besked.
english: The person in question has not responded.
tip: "Vederbörande" = the person in question. Very formal.

target: Förra veckan reste vi till Kiruna.
english: Last week we traveled to Kiruna.
tip: "Förra" = last: förra veckan, förra året, förra gången.

target: Aldrig har jag sett något sådant.
english: Never have I seen anything like it.
tip: Starting with "aldrig" creates emphasis and triggers V2 inversion.

target: Hemma hos oss firar vi alltid jul.
english: At our home we always celebrate Christmas.
tip: In writing, `dem` is the standard object form for 'them' – but in speech, Swedes often say `dom` for both subject and object. Spelling stays formal.

target: I helgen ska vi åka till stugan.
english: On the weekend we're going to the cabin.
tip: "Stugan" = the cottage. Many Swedes have a "stuga" for weekends and holidays.

target: Under sommaren badar vi i sjön verkligen.
english: During the summer we actually swim in the lake.
tip: "Under" + time = during: "under sommaren" = during summer.

target: Hur önskar ni betala väldigt ofta nog?
english: How would you like to pay very often probably?
tip: Formal customer service Swedish.

target: Var hon bor är en hemlighet med familjen.
english: Where she lives is a secret with the family.
tip: Indirect question as subject: "Var hon bor" = where she lives.

target: Vad vacker hon var på stationen varje morgon!
english: How beautiful she was at the station every morning!
tip: Exclamatory word order: "Vad" + adjective + subject + verb.
